children: Raw sugar futures on ICE rose for a fourth straight session to hit a one-week high on Wednesday, while arabica coffee headed back toward a three-month low.
rose 0.5% to 17.84 cents per lb at 1232 GMT, having hit a high of 18.02.

* "We are seeing more rain-related crush delays and there is more rain expected in the first week of October. The market might still test 18.60," said independent broker and consultant Michael McDougall.
* He also noted that rising oil prices are driving sugar higher, but added that against that, bit added demand remains weak.

* India, for example, is moving closer to new regulations to restrict the sale of foods high in fat and sugar within a 50-metre radius of schools, the latest proposal to cut the consumption of junk food in the country.
fell 0.6% to $2.6665 per lb, heading back toward Tuesday's three-month low of $2.6300.

* Top grower Brazil's 2026 coffee crop is expected to total a record 67.6 million 60-kg bags, national crop agency Conab said, raising its estimate from 66.7 million as stronger arabica yields more than offset lower robusta production.
fell 1% to $3,284 a metric ton after slumping to a 3-1/2-month low of $3,218 on Tuesday.
* "Healthy supplies from Brazil and steadily rising exports from Vietnam are putting pressure on robusta prices," said a trader based in top robusta grower Vietnam.
* Broker ADMIS said rains are expected to continue over the next ten days in top grower West Africa, easing concerns over the upcoming 2026/27 crop.
